task: How do different strategies for enforcing prediction symmetry affect accuracy when using NLI-based and zero-shot models for paraphrase detection on MRPC?
key_finding: The effect of bidirectional symmetry enforcement is highly model-family dependent and does not uniformly improve accuracy. For zero-shot NLI pipelines, bidirectional averaging slightly hurts performance relative to single-direction scoring (acc ~0.613 vs ~0.630). For the fine-tuned HF pipeline, the effect is negligible (acc ~0.850 vs ~0.858). Only for the cross-encoder does bidirectional averaging provide a modest gain (acc ~0.699 vs ~0.679). Among aggregation strategies, average-margin outperforms min-direction by a large margin (acc ~0.703 vs ~0.586 for direct NLI); min-direction is overly conservative and collapses recall. The agent should compare aggregation strategies within each family and note that improvements from bidirectionality are more pronounced for cross-encoders than for NLI or zero-shot models. Flan-T5 (flan_t5_symmetric_prompt_average_mrpc) uses a generative symmetry strategy (averaging yes/no logits for both prompt orderings) and achieves acc ~0.738, F1 ~0.807, representing a distinct symmetry approach outside the NLI/pipeline families.

rating.rationale: Only agent to meet the minimum coverage, explicitly citing hf_pipeline_mrpc_bidirectional_order_average, softmax_gap_mean_mrpc, consensus_then_avg_margin_mrpc, min_direction_margin_mrpc, neutral_penalized_margin_mrpc, and flan_t5_symmetric_prompt_average_mrpc. Correctly reports that HF bidirectional averaging is nearly neutral/slightly worse and that min-direction style symmetry is overly conservative and harms recall. However, it misses direct_nli_entailment_mrpc, bidirectional_averaged_zero_shot_mrpc, and quora_cross_encoder_symmetric_average_mrpc, so it does not fully recover the model-family-dependent picture, and it somewhat conflates fine-tuned HF and direct-NLI results.
